1.why: MFA routes resolve the account solely via accountForSession(session) after getSession(req, "authenticated"), with no client-supplied account id.

2.why: Identity OTPs are bound to the pending session’s identityCodeHash and accountId; TOTP/backup codes are per-account, so one user’s code does not authenticate another.

3.why: Enabling MFA only updates account.mfa and never deletes or revokes other entries in the sessions map, so prior sessions remain valid.

4.why: TOTP secret is stored as AES-GCM encryptedTotpSecret; backup codes are stored only as SHA-256 hashes with serverPepper.

5.why: Tokens, secrets, and codes use crypto.getRandomValues / secureInt (rejection sampling), not Math.random.

6.why: Session id is only in the __Host-mfa_session HttpOnly cookie; client code uses memory variables, not localStorage/sessionStorage or non-HttpOnly cookies.

7.why: Server validates email, phone, OTP shape, and recovery-code format; body size/type are bounded; no string-built queries exist.

8.why: Dynamic values are applied with textContent/message(); API responses are JSON; HTML shells are static templates without unescaped user input.

9.why: Handler never issues redirects or Location headers; only allow-listed paths are served and query strings are rejected.

10.why: headersFor sets CSP (frame-ancestors 'none'), HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, and X-Frame-Options: DENY on responses.

11.why: cookieHeader sets HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict on the __Host-mfa_session cookie.

12.why: Errors use genericError without stack traces; secrets are not written to logs or URLs (query strings rejected); catch returns generic 500.

13.why: Identity codes are single-use (identityUsed) and time-bound (identityExpiresAt); TOTP counters resist replay; backup codes flip used=true.

14.why: Identity, TOTP, and recovery paths increment failure counters and set lockUntil after VERIFICATION_FAILURE_THRESHOLD, returning 429.

15.why: rotateAuthenticatedSession issues a new session id/csrf; idle/absolute timeouts are enforced in getSession; logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
